title: Marked trivializations of flat smooth affine deformations lift across nilpotent quotients
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $R$ be a commutative $k$-algebra, and let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal with $I^N=0$ for some $N\geq1$. Put $R_0=R/I$. Let $T$ be an affine $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme] smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and for any commutative $k$-algebra $B$ write $T_B=T\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $D\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a flat scheme [def-weil-flat-morphism]. For every $R_0$-isomorphism $\theta_0:D\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}R_0\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{R_0}$ there exists an $R$-isomorphism $\theta:D\xrightarrow{\sim}T_R$ whose base change to $R_0$ is $\theta_0$. No affineness or finite-presentation hypothesis is imposed on $D$. The empty affine scheme $T$ and the zero base ring are allowed.

source.place: Tags 06AD (lemma-thickening-affine-scheme) and 02H0 (definition-formally-smooth): relative marked-trivialization consequence for a smooth affine target and a flat source. This is the affine lifting input behind examples-defos.tex, Tag 0DZN (lemma-glueing-smooth); the direct ring argument is recorded in the worker report.

proof.text: Put $D_j=D\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}(R/I^j)$ for $1\le j\le N$. Write $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$. The affine fibre-product lemma makes $T_{R/I}$ affine, so $D_1$ is affine via $\theta_0$. For $1\le j<N$, the kernel $I^j/I^{j+1}$ of $R/I^{j+1}\to R/I^j$ has square zero, since $2j\ge j+1$. Its spectral closed immersion is a first order thickening. By the universal property of fibre products, $D_{j+1}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(R/I^{j+1})}\operatorname{Spec}(R/I^j)\cong D_j$ over $D_{j+1}$, so the first-order base-change lemma makes $D_j\hookrightarrow D_{j+1}$ a first order thickening, hence a thickening. Apply affineness under thickenings successively to obtain affine $D_N=D$. This argument imposes neither finite presentation nor affineness on $D$ in advance.

Choose $D=\operatorname{Spec}C$ over $R$. The affine flatness criterion applied to its given structure morphism says that $C$ is flat as an $R$-module. Put $J=IC$; then $J^N=0$. The affine fibre-product and quotient-tensor identifications give $D_1=\operatorname{Spec}(C/J)$ and $T_R=\operatorname{Spec}P$ with $P=A\otimes_kR$. Under these identifications the specified $\theta_0$ corresponds contravariantly to an $R/I$-algebra isomorphism $\alpha_0:A\otimes_k(R/I)\xrightarrow{\sim}C/J$. Set $u_1(a)=\alpha_0(a\otimes1)$.

source.place: Tag 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize); Schemes Tags 01I4/01JQ; Algebra Tag 00DF quotient-tensor calculation

proof.text: Smoothness of $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ includes formal smoothness. By the affine formal-smoothness equivalence, $A$ has the square-zero lifting property for $k$-algebra maps. Starting with $u_1:A\to C/J$, construct compatible $u_j:A\to C/J^j$ for $1\le j\le N$: at the induction step apply that property to $C/J^{j+1}\twoheadrightarrow C/J^j$, whose kernel $J^j/J^{j+1}$ has square zero because $2j\ge j+1$. Thus $u=u_N:A\to C$ reduces to $u_1$ modulo $J$. Define the $R$-algebra map $\alpha:P\to C$ by $\alpha(a\otimes r)=u(a)r$. Its reduction $P/IP\to C/IC$ equals $\alpha_0$: both send $a\otimes\bar r$ to $u_1(a)\bar r$.

source.place: Tags 02H0 (definition-formally-smooth), 02H4 (lemma-affine-formally-smooth); explicit iteration over powers of J

proof.text: The map $\alpha$ is surjective. Indeed its reduction modulo $I$ is the isomorphism $\alpha_0$, so $C=\alpha(P)+IC$. Apply nilpotent Nakayama to the $R$-linear map $\alpha:P\to C$. This version requires no finite generation.

For any $R$-module $M$, identify $(R/I)\otimes_RM$ with $M/IM$ explicitly: $\bar r\otimes m\mapsto rm\bmod IM$, with inverse $m\bmod IM\mapsto\bar1\otimes m$. The first map is well-defined by bilinearity and the second because $\bar1\otimes im=\bar i\otimes m=0$ for $i\in I$. The two composites are identities on the indicated generators. These formulas identify a tensored module homomorphism with its induced quotient map.

source.place: Tag 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact), quotient-tensor identification from the defining bilinear relations

proof.text: Let $K=\ker\alpha$. By step 4, $0\to K\to P\xrightarrow{\alpha}C\to0$ is short exact over $R$, and $C$ is $R$-flat by step 2. The flat-quotient tensor lemma with $N=R/I$ gives an exact sequence $0\to(R/I)\otimes_RK\to(R/I)\otimes_RP\to(R/I)\otimes_RC\to0$. By step 5 this is $0\to K/IK\to P/IP\xrightarrow{\alpha_0}C/IC\to0$. Since $\alpha_0$ is injective, $K/IK=0$, hence $K=IK$. Nilpotent Nakayama applied to $K$ gives $K=0$. Thus $\alpha$ is bijective. We used flatness of $C$ over $R$, without assuming flatness of the map $P\to C$.

The inverse of the bijective $R$-algebra map $\alpha$ preserves addition, multiplication, unit and $R$-scalars by applying $\alpha$ to each required identity. Taking spectra gives $\theta:D\xrightarrow{\sim}T_R$. Its reduction is $\theta_0$: by the affine fibre-product lemma (projections are spectra of $c\mapsto c\otimes1$ and $\bar r\mapsto1\otimes\bar r$) and the uniqueness in the universal property of fibre products, the base change $\theta\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ is, under the identifications of step 2, the spectrum of $\alpha\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_{R/I}$, which the quotient-tensor identification turns into the reduction $P/IP\to C/IC$ of $\alpha$; this is exactly $\alpha_0$ by step 3, and morphisms of affine spectra are determined by their ring maps. For $N=1$ the two inductions have no steps and $I=0$. If $T$ is empty then $A=0$, $C/IC=0$ and nilpotent Nakayama gives $C=0$, so both schemes are empty. If $R=0$, every $R$-algebra is zero and both schemes are empty as well.

source.place: Affine-spectrum correspondence (Tag 01I2, lemma-category-affine-schemes); nilpotent Nakayama (Algebra Tag 00DV) for the empty cases; Schemes Tags 01I4/01JQ for the base change of an affine morphism
